what_happened: Found an explicit L-plus marker gadget (theta := not-m AND allFuture m pins the evaluation point exactly; nu := theta OR F theta marks the closed past) that lets the open-future modal's existential dual express a gap-anchored past property Delta-prime that U/S cannot reach. This converts route R3a from 'find a bisimulation' into a concrete, compiled computation plus a GHR-12.4.2-style collapse argument over Q-time.

Discovered mid-round that the frame-constraint Limit blocks the naive 'permissive Q-frame' the negative construction needed: at a frame whose states are the atom colours alone, distinct states must be unrelated at all small durations, so over a dense duration a finitely-many-states history is a uniformly-discrete step function with no accumulating run structure. Resolved by routing through the repository's own colourClock (Semantics/Frames/TranslationProduct.lean), whose clock component discharges Limit while leaving the colour component free; colourFibre + its IsRegular instance compile. A second, smaller cost: the colourClock wrapper's internal Nonempty instance blocks ofReflectiveRegular_taskRel from unifying, so the 'every colour function is a history' step stayed a one-line audited paper step instead of compiling.
